Mahjong Game Rules

Mahjong is a game where players pull and discard tiles. The player starts with 13 tiles and you pull one tile from the stack and discard one tile that you don’t need. You need to form hands in a specific pattern to make your hand have meaning and grant you points once you're out. If your hand is complete you can say you're done and depending on how rare your hand is you are given points from other players. You can see the tiles other players discarded as well so it can give you clues on what hands they are making. You can also take action against the tiles other players discard. If you can form one pattern using a tile another player discards you can “call” and take it to form one of the patterns required to make certain hands. You can also do something called “Ron” which is when you complete your hand with the tile another person discards, with this you can make the person who discarded that tile pay all of the points you would gain from your hand instead of the regular where everyone pays their share. Akagi starts this game in a point disadvantage so now he ideally wants to take a “Ron” from Urabe to directly take points from him. The players with money on the line are Akagi and Urabe, and the winning condition from either side is that the side who loses all of their points loses.
General shape of a hand:
You have one head which is just two of the same tiles
You have 4 of either shuntsu or coutsu
Shuntsu is 3 tiles that are in numerical order, and it has to be the same tile, so for example 3man, 4man, 5man will be one shuntsu
Coutsu is 3 tiles that are the same, like 3man, 3man, 3man. Also all tiles that are symbol based can only make Coutsu or the head as they do not have numerical order
There are many types of Yaku you can make with this general shape
For a deeper understanding it's better to just learn Mahjong
Types of tiles :
There are 3 types of number tiles, manzu, pinzu, and souzu
If I am referring to a manzu tile with the number 3 I will say 3man, if it's souzu 3 sou, if it's pinzu 3 pin.

There are also tiles that have directions written in it like south east west north. There are also tiles that have a blank, middle, or departure kanji written on it. Forming various patterns with these tiles creates hands and if it forms a clear pattern with lower chance its generally likely that its a powerful hand, here is a link to all the types of Yaku :
https://riichi.wiki/List_of_yaku
These Yaku’s can be combined too to make more powerful hands, generally the more Yaku you have the higher the score of your hand.
